newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt denies budget spending reports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt denies budget spending reports.

text.p: The Australian government rejected on Friday reports that it intended to significantly boost budget spending in the 1997/98 financial year, saying its budget spending programme was not yet finalised.
A spokesman for Acting Treasurer John Fahey said newspaper reports that the May 23 budget would provide for A$1.0 billion in new infrastructure spending were not based on fact.
"It's pre-budget speculation and we can't give it any weight," the spokesman said.
"I think it's basically cobbled together from various (rumours) that they may have heard about the place."
The spokesman said there was still a great deal of work to be done ahead of the budget and many changes were still likely to be made.
"There's certainly nothing set in concrete as far as what will be in the next budget," he said.
He said the government's mid-year budget review, due out in late January, would not contain spending programme details but would identify the macro-economic framework for the budget.
